akhfash:2-2.t: He said ﴿جَمَعَ﴾ and ﴿جَمَعَ مَالاً وَعَدَّدَهُ﴾: from "العِدَّة" (number, counting).

akhfash:3-4.t: [And He said] ﴿يَحْسَبُ أَنَّ مَالَهُ أَخْلَدَهُ﴾ ﴿كَلاَّ لَيُنبَذَنَّ فِي ٱلْحُطَمَةِ﴾, that is: he and his wealth.

akhfash:8-8.t: And He said ﴿مُّؤْصَدَةٌ﴾: from "أَأْصَدَ" "يُؤصِدُ"; and some say "أُوْصِدَتْ", and that one is not pronounced with hamza, like "أَوْجَعَ", so "مُوجع". Similarly "أَأْكَفَ" and "أَوْكَفَ" — both are said.

celaleyn:1-1.t: ﴿وَيْلٌ﴾: a word of punishment, or a valley in Hell, ﴿لِكُلِّ هُمَزَةٍ لُمَزَةٍ﴾, that is, one much given to hamz and lamz, that is, backbiting. It was revealed concerning those who used to backbite the Prophet ﷺ and the believers, such as Umayya ibn Khalaf, al-Walīd ibn al-Mughīra and others,

celaleyn:2-2.t: ﴿الَّذِي جَمَعَ﴾ — with the lightened and with the doubled [mīm] — ﴿مَالًا وَعَدَّدَهُ﴾: counted it and made it a provision against the misfortunes of time.

celaleyn:3-3.t: ﴿يَحْسَبُ﴾, in his ignorance, ﴿أَنَّ مَالَهُ أَخْلَدَهُ﴾: made him immortal, never to die.

celaleyn:4-4.t: ﴿كَلَّا﴾: a deterrent (radʿ). ﴿لَيُنْبَذَنَّ﴾: the answer to an omitted oath, that is, he will surely be thrown ﴿فِي الْحُطَمَةِ﴾, which crushes everything thrown into it.

celaleyn:7-7.t: ﴿الَّتِي تَطَّلِعُ﴾: rises over ﴿عَلَى الْأَفْئِدَةِ﴾: the hearts, and burns them; their pain is more intense than the pain of other [parts] because of their delicacy.

celaleyn:8-8.t: ﴿إِنَّهَا عَلَيْهِمْ﴾ — the pronoun is plural in observance of the meaning of «كل» — ﴿مُؤْصَدَةٌ﴾ — with hamza, and with wāw in its place — closed over,

celaleyn:9-9.t: ﴿فِي عُمُدٍ﴾ — with ḍamma on the two letters, and with fatḥa on them [عَمَدٍ] — ﴿مُمَدَّدَةٍ﴾: a ṣifa (adjective) of what precedes it; so the Fire is inside the columns.

daas-irab:1-1.t: ﴿وَيْلٌ﴾ mubtadaʾ (subject), in the nominative (marfūʿ). ﴿لِكُلِّ﴾ its khabar (predicate). ﴿هُمَزَةٍ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿لُمَزَةٍ﴾ a badal (substitute) from it; the clause is initial (ibtidāʾiyya), with no grammatical position.

daas-irab:2-2.t: ﴿الَّذِي﴾ a relative noun, a badal (substitute) of the whole for the whole (badal kull min kull). ﴿جَمَعَ﴾ a past verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir). ﴿مالًا﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause is the ṣila (relative clause). ﴿وَعَدَّدَهُ﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to what precedes it.

daas-irab:3-3.t: ﴿يَحْسَبُ﴾ an imperfect verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir). ﴿أَنَّ مالَهُ﴾ anna and its noun. ﴿أَخْلَدَهُ﴾ a past verb and its object, and the fāʿil is latent; the clause is the khabar (predicate) of anna, and the interpreted maṣdar (maṣdar muʾawwal) formed from anna and what follows it stands in place of the two objects of يحسب; the clause «يحسب..» is a ḥāl (circumstantial).

daas-irab:4-4.t: ﴿كَلَّا﴾ a particle of deterrence and rebuke (radʿ wa-zajr). ﴿لَيُنْبَذَنَّ﴾ the lām occurs in the response to an omitted oath, and a passive imperfect verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa because it is attached to the heavy nūn of emphasis; the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) is latent (mustatir), and the clause is the response to the oath, with no grammatical position. ﴿فِي الْحُطَمَةِ﴾ attached to (mutaʿalliq) what precedes them.

daas-irab:6-6.t: ﴿نارُ اللَّهِ﴾ the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), and the Name of Majesty is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿الْمُوقَدَةُ﴾ an adjective (ṣifa) of نار; the clause is a badal (substitute) from الحطمة.

daas-irab:7-7.t: ﴿الَّتِي﴾ a relative noun, an adjective (ṣifa) of نار. ﴿تَطَّلِعُ﴾ an imperfect verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); the clause is the ṣila (relative clause). ﴿عَلَى الْأَفْئِدَةِ﴾ attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb.

daas-irab:8-8.t: ﴿إِنَّها﴾ inna and its noun. ﴿عَلَيْهِمْ﴾ attached to (mutaʿalliq) the khabar (predicate). ﴿مُؤْصَدَةٌ﴾ khabar; the nominal clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial).

daas-irab:9-9.t: ﴿فِي عَمَدٍ﴾ the preposition and its genitive noun are an adjective (ṣifa) of مؤصدة. ﴿مُمَدَّدَةٍ﴾ an adjective of عمد.

dervis-irab:1-9.t:
* Vocabulary:
(هُمَزَةٍ): In al-Mukhtār: «al-hamz is like al-lamz in pattern and meaning, and its verb-class is that of ḍaraba.» Also in it: «al-lamz is finding fault; its origin is signalling with the eye and the like; its verb-class is that of ḍaraba and naṣara.» The tāʾ in both is for intensification of the description. It has preceded that the pattern fuʿala, with ḍamma on the fāʾ and fatḥa on the ʿayn, is for intensification of the agent, i.e. one who does much of what the word is derived from, and the pattern fuʿla, with ḍamma on the fāʾ and sukūn on the ʿayn, is for intensification of the object. One says «رجل لُعَنة» (luʿana), with ḍamma on the lām and fatḥa on the ʿayn, of one who curses others much, and «لُعْنة» (luʿna), with ḍamma on the lām and sukūn on the ʿayn, when he is cursed by people, who curse him much. Al-Samīn's wording: «The generality [of readers] read both with fatḥa on the mīm, meaning the person from whom that act comes much; the others read with sukūn, meaning the one who [gives cause to be] slandered and backbitten, i.e. who brings what he is slandered and backbitten for — like ḍuḥaka of one who laughs much and ḍuḥka of one who does what is laughed at. It is regular, I mean that fuʿala with fatḥa on the ʿayn is for one from whom the act comes much, and with sukūn for one on account of whom the act occurs much.»
Ibn Khālawayh's wording: «The hāʾ [tāʾ marbūṭa] in "همزة" entered for intensification of blame, as in their saying "rajul humaza lumaza", i.e. a fault-finder and backbiter; and "rajul farūqa, ṣakhkhāba, jakhkhāba": one of much talk and quarrelling; "naqqāqa, mihdhāra, halbāja". Al-Aṣmaʿī said: I asked a Bedouin about the halbāja and he said: he is the tall, bulky fool, very meddlesome, gluttonous, ill-mannered — and if you stopped [me], I would [go on] describing him until tomorrow; there is nothing among faults worse than the halbāja. Since the hāʾ entered for that [purpose], masculine and feminine became equal, so it is said "a woman humaza" and "a man humaza", "a woman farūqa" and "a man farūqa", and it is not put in the dual or plural: one says "men humaza" and "women humaza". The grammarians said: when they put the hāʾ on [an epithet of] one who is praised, they take it in the sense of the shrewd one possessed of irba, which is intelligence, as it is said "rajul ʿallāma" and "nassāba"; and when they put the hāʾ on [an epithet of] one who is blamed, they take it in the sense of the beast. Similar is His saying "بل الإنسان على نفسه بصيرة": the hāʾ is for intensification; and similar is the saying of the Exalted "ولا تزال تطلع على خائنة منهم": the hāʾ is for intensification. And he recited:
تدلي بودّي إذا لاقيتني كذبا ... وإن أغيب فأنت الهافر اللمزه
(You falsely lay claim to my affection when you meet me, but if I am absent, you are the backbiter, the fault-finder.)
Al-hāfir is the backbiter and al-lāmiz is the fault-finder. Allah the Exalted said: "ومنهم من يلمزك في الصدقات", i.e. strikes at you (yuṣībuka).» [Translator's note: «يصيبك» as printed; «يعيبك» (finds fault with you) would be expected.] What we have extracted from the books of language is the following inflection of the two.
One says: hamazahu yahmuzuhu (with ḍamma on the mīm) and yahmizuhu (with kasra), hamzan: he poked him, pressed him, prodded him, pushed him, struck him, bit him, and backbit him in his absence; so he is hammāz and humaza, [like] kasra [Translator's note: so in the text; the pattern-word is presumably a misprint]. Hamaza al-shayṭānu al-insāna: he whispered an insinuation into his heart. Hamaza bihi al-arḍa: he threw him to the ground. Hamaza al-farasa: he prodded the horse with the spur (al-mihmāz) so that it would run. Hamaza al-ʿinaba or its head: he pressed it. Hamaza al-kalimata or al-ḥarfa: he pronounced it with a hamza or put the sign of the hamza on it.
And one says: lamazahu yalmuzuhu (with ḍamma on the mīm) and yalmizuhu (with kasra), lamzan: he found fault with him, signalled at him with his eye and the like together with hidden speech, pushed him and struck him; lamazahu al-shaybu: grey hair appeared in him. Saʿīd ibn Jubayr said: «Al-humaza is the one who strikes (yahmizu) people with his hand and beats them, and al-lumaza is the one who slanders (yalmizu) them with his tongue and finds fault with them.» Ibn Kaysān said: al-humaza is the one who hurts his companion with foul speech, and al-lumaza is the one who winks his eye, gestures with his head and signals with his eyebrow. There are other views, all of which go back to a single root, namely attacking and exposing faults.
(عَدَّدَهُ): Al-Shihāb al-Ḥalabī, known as al-Samīn, said: «The generality [of readers] read with the first dāl doubled, which is also for intensification; al-Ḥasan and al-Kalbī read it lightened. Whoever doubled its mīm looked to intensification and multiplication, and whoever lightened its mīm made it admit multiplication and its absence.» [Translator's note: «ميمه» (its mīm) as printed; the letter in question is the dāl.] The meaning is: he amassed it, kept count of it and reckoned it up.
(لَيُنْبَذَنَّ): he will surely be thrown. Ibn Khālawayh's wording: «The meaning of "ينبذن" is: he will be left in Hell. Allah the Exalted said: "فنبذوه وراء ظهورهم", i.e. they left it. The foundling child (al-ṣabiyy al-manbūdh) is the one left [abandoned]; he is [also called] the child of motion, al-mudaghdagh, and the son of the night, i.e. the child of the wicked woman; and he is al-nufl and the son of al-musāʿāt — all of it [meaning] the child of fornication.»
(الْحُطَمَةِ): one of the names of the Fire, i.e. that which smashes everything thrown into it. In al-Mukhtār: «ḥaṭamahu, of the verb-class of ḍaraba, i.e. he broke it, so it broke (inḥaṭama, taḥaṭṭama); al-taḥṭīm is breaking; al-ḥuṭama is one of the names of the Fire, because it smashes what it swallows.»
(مُؤْصَدَةٌ): closed over. [The poet] said:
تحنّ إلى جبال مكة ناقتي ... ومن دونها أبواب صنعاء مؤصدة
(My she-camel yearns for the mountains of Mecca, while before them the gates of Ṣanʿāʾ are shut.)
(عَمَدٍ): it was read with two fatḥas, with two ḍammas, and with ḍamma then sukūn. The first two are plurals of ʿamūd. In the books of language: al-ʿamūd is that on which the house and other things stand, and a rod of iron; the plural is aʿmida, ʿamad and ʿumud. The third is a lightening of the reading ʿumud with two ḍammas. Ibn Khālawayh's wording: «Al-ʿamad is the plural of ʿamūd. Nothing has come in the speech of the Arabs on this pattern except four words: adīm and adam, ʿamūd and ʿamad, afīq and afaq, ihāb and ahab. Al-Farrāʾ added a fifth: qaḍīm and qaḍam, meaning parchments and skins. The people of Kufa read "في عُمُد" with two ḍammas, which is also the plural of ʿamūd, like rasūl and rusul. Hārūn related from Abū ʿAmr "في عُمْد" with sukūn on the mīm, as a lightening, like rasūl and rusl.»

* I'rab:
(وَيْلٌ لِكُلِّ هُمَزَةٍ لُمَزَةٍ الَّذِي جَمَعَ مالًا وَعَدَّدَهُ): «ويل» is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and «لكل همزة» is its khabar (predicate). What permitted beginning with it although it is indefinite is the sense it contains of invoking destruction upon them. Ibn Khālawayh's wording: «If someone asks: "ويل" is indefinite, and one does not begin with an indefinite noun, so what accounts for the nominative? Say: when the indefinite comes close to the definite, it is fit to begin with, as in "Better than Zayd is a man of the Banū Tamīm" and "A man in the house is standing". Likewise the interrogative alif makes beginning with the indefinite easy, as in His saying [sic] "أمنطلق أخوك". This is one view. Others said: "ويل" is definite, because it is the name of a valley in Hell — we seek refuge with Allah from it. If it is said: Did the Arabs know that? Say: the words of the Qurʾān come as an Arabic word used figuratively, just as Allah the Exalted called the idol "Baʿl" when it was taken as a lord, and called the idol "punishment" and "rujz", saying "والرجز فاهجر", because whoever worships the idol is struck by the rujz (punishment), so it was named by the name of what it causes. So since al-wayl is destruction and ruin, and whoever enters the Fire has perished, it is permissible to call the destination of al-wayl "wayl". Likewise "فسوف يلقون غيا" — it is said to be a valley in Hell, we seek refuge with Allah from it. In grammar "ويلاً لكل همزة" is permissible as an invocation, i.e. may Allah make woe cling to him. Jarīr said:
كسا اللؤم تيما خضرة في جلودها ... فويلا لتيم من سرابيلها الخضر
(Baseness has clothed Taym with a greenness in their skins, so woe to Taym from its green shirts!)
— with the accusative, the correct transmission. The Kufans allowed wayl, wayli, waylu and waylan, whether the annexation is cut off or intended. Al-ways is a word lighter than al-wayl, al-wayḥ is a word lighter than al-ways, and al-wayb is a word lighter than al-wayḥ: "wayl li-Zayd", "waylahu", "wayḥahu", "waysahu", "waybahu". When it stands alone, the nominative and the accusative are both permissible; when it is annexed, it can only be accusative, because it would remain without a khabar; and when it is separated, you make the lām [phrase] the khabar. Al-Ḥasan said: "wayḥ" is a word of mercy. If it is said: how is a verb inflected from wayḥ, ways and wayl? Say: the Arabs did not inflect a verb from them. As for this fabricated verse:
فما وال وما واح ... وما واس أبو زيد
(Abū Zayd did not say "wayl", nor "wayḥ", nor "ways".)
— pay no attention to it, for it is a vile fabrication.»
«لمزة» is a badal (substitute) of «همزة». This is Ibn Khālawayh's wording: «"لمزة" is a substitute of it. Al-mihmaza is a stick with a piece of iron at its tip, carried by the horse-breaker, with which he prods the riding animal; the plural is mahāmiz. ʿAdī said, describing a horse:
نصفه جوزه نصير شواه ... مكرم من مهامز الرّوّاض
(We describe its middle [?] and its legs; it is spared the spurs of the horse-breakers.) [Translator's note: the first hemistich is obscure as printed; the gloss is tentative.]
And Abū Muḥallim recited:
هل غير همز ولمز للصديق ولا ... ينكي عدوكم منكم أظافير»
(Is there anything but prodding and slandering of the friend, while your enemy is not wounded by any claws of yours?)
It is also said [that «لمزة»] is a verbal tawkīd (emphasis) of «همزة» by a synonym. «الذي» is a badal of «كل», a substitution of a definite for an indefinite, or it is accusative by an omitted verb, as blame. Ibn Khālawayh parsed it as a naʿt (adjective) of «كل همزة لمزة», and that is not far-fetched. The clause «جمع» is the ṣila (relative clause) of «الذي», with no grammatical position; the agent of «جمع» is latent, its implied form being «هو», referring to «كل همزة لمزة»; «مالا» is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); and «عدده» is conjoined to «جمع». Ibn Khālawayh's wording: «"وعدده" is coordinated (nasaq) with it; the maṣdar is ʿaddada yuʿaddidu taʿdīdan, so he is muʿaddid; and the hāʾ is a direct object. Al-Ḥasan read "جمع مالا وعَدَدَه" lightened, i.e. he amassed wealth and knew its number and reckoned it up. Whoever lightened it made al-ʿadad a maṣdar and a noun, and whoever doubled it made it a past verb.» This is one view on the meaning of the lightened [reading]. It is also said: and he gathered his own ʿadad (supporting numbers) of his clan and kinsmen; on this interpretation it is likewise a noun, conjoined to «مالا», i.e. and he amassed the number of the wealth, or the number of his own [people]. It is also said that «عدده» [lightened] is a past verb meaning «عدّه» (he counted it), except that it is anomalous in being left unassimilated, the regular form being assimilation, just as the poet was anomalous in his saying: «إني أجود لأقوام وإن ضنّوا» (I am generous to people even if they are stingy) — i.e. bakhilū [with «ضننوا» unassimilated in the original].
(يَحْسَبُ أَنَّ مالَهُ أَخْلَدَهُ): the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the agent of «جمع», i.e. reckoning and supposing that wealth will make him immortal, i.e. bring him to the rank of immortality so that he will not die. It may also be resumptive, an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī) answering a question, as if it were said: what is the matter with him that he amasses wealth and is concerned with it? «أن» and its noun, and the clause «أخلده» is its khabar; and «أن» with what is in its domain stands in place of the two objects of «يحسب». In al-Mukhtār: «al-khuld, with ḍamma, is permanence; its verb-class is that of dakhala; akhladahu Allāhu and khalladahu takhlīdan.»
(كَلَّا لَيُنْبَذَنَّ فِي الْحُطَمَةِ وَما أَدْراكَ مَا الْحُطَمَةُ نارُ اللَّهِ الْمُوقَدَةُ): «كلا» is deterrence and rebuke of him for his supposition, i.e. the matter is not as passed through his mind, that wealth will make him immortal. The lām is the answer to an omitted oath; «ينبذنّ» is an imperfect passive verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on fatḥa because of its being attached to the heavy nūn of emphasis; its nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) is latent, its implied form being «هو»; the clause has no grammatical position because it is the answer to the oath; and «في الحطمة» is attached (mutaʿalliq) to «ينبذنّ». The wāw is a conjunction; «ما» is an interrogative noun in the position of a nominative, mubtadaʾ; the clause «أدراك» is a verbal clause in the position of a nominative, khabar; «ما» is an interrogative noun, mubtadaʾ, and «الحطمة» is the khabar; and the nominal clause, suspended [from the verb] by the interrogative, stands in place of the second object of «أدراك». Many parallels to it have preceded. «نار الله» is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, i.e. «هي نار الله», and «الموقدة» is an adjective of «النار». Ibn Khālawayh allowed it to be a badal of «الحطمة», with «الموقدة» an adjective of «نار الله». His wording:
«"نار الله الموقدة": if you wish, you make "النار" a substitute; and if you wish, you make it nominative as the khabar of an implied mubtadaʾ, i.e. "هي نار الله". The name of Allah the Exalted is genitive by annexation, and "الموقدة" is an adjective of "النار"; its pattern is mufʿala, from awqadtu, ūqidu, īqādan, so I am mūqid and the fire is mūqada. And the fire itself waqadat, taqidu, waqdan and wuqūdan (with ḍamma on the wāw), so it is wāqida. Allah the Exalted said: "وقودها الناس والحجارة", meaning sulphur stones; al-waqūd with fatḥa is firewood. Ṭalḥa read "وُقودها" with ḍamma on the wāw, making it a maṣdar. The poet — Ḥātim al-Ṭāʾī — said:
ليلك يا موقد ليل قرّ ... والريح مع ذلك ريح صرّ
أوقد يرى نارك من يمرّ ... إن جلبت ضيفا فأنت حر
(O kindler of the fire, your night is a cold night, and the wind besides is a biting wind; kindle [it], so that whoever passes may see your fire — if you bring in a guest, you are free.)
This is the best that has been said on its meaning.»
(الَّتِي تَطَّلِعُ عَلَى الْأَفْئِدَةِ): «التي» is an adjective of «النار»; it may also be in the position of a nominative, as the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ. The clause «تطّلع» is the ṣila of «التي», with no grammatical position; the agent of «تطّلع» is «هي», referring to the Fire; and «على الأفئدة» is attached to «تطّلع». The pattern of «تطّلع» is tafṭaʿil: the tāʾ of iftiʿāl was changed to ṭāʾ because it came after a ṭāʾ; it is likewise changed to ṭāʾ when [the first radical] is ṣād, ḍād or ẓāʾ. ʿUrwa ibn Udhayna said:
عاود القلب خيال ردعه ... كلما قلت تناهى اطلعه
يا له داء ترى صاحبه ... ساهم الوجه له ممتقعه
(A phantom returned to the heart, a phantom that had been held back; whenever I said it had ceased, it came to view again. What a malady! You see the one afflicted by it with a lean face, pallid on its account.)
(إِنَّها عَلَيْهِمْ مُؤْصَدَةٌ فِي عَمَدٍ مُمَدَّدَةٍ): «إن» and its noun; «عليهم» is attached to «مؤصدة»; «في عمد» is an adjective of «مؤصدة» — this is the view Abū al-Baqāʾ took, so that the Fire is inside the columns. It is also said [it is attached] to an omitted [word], the khabar of an implied mubtadaʾ. Al-Samīn preferred that it be a ḥāl of the pronoun in «عليهم», i.e. bound fast. «ممددة» is an adjective of «العمد».

* Rhetoric:
In His saying «لينبذنّ في الحطمة» after «ويل لكل همزة لمزة» there is a verbal correspondence (muqābala lafẓiyya) of splendid eloquence. For when He branded him with this mark, in a form indicating that it is deep-rooted in him and has taken firm hold of him, He followed the repeated intensification in «الهمزة» and «اللمزة» with His threat of the Fire, which He named «الحطمة» because of the terror he suffers in it and the punishment he meets in it. In specifying it He chose an intensive form on the pattern of the form in which He couched the sin committed, so that equivalence is achieved between sin and recompense: this one who became addicted to sin, his recompense is this ḥuṭama, which is also ravenous, smashing everything thrown into it. It is said that this sūra was revealed about al-Akhnas ibn Sharīq, whose habit was backbiting and slander; it is also said about Umayya ibn Khalaf; and it is said about al-Walīd ibn al-Mughīra and his backbiting of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and his disparagement of him. Even if the occasion was specific, the threat was general, covering everyone who bears this base mark, so that it functions as an innuendo (taʿrīḍ) at the one about whom it was revealed, for that is a stronger deterrent to him and wounds him more deeply. The discussion of taʿrīḍ has passed: it consists in a person alluding by one thing to another without stating it explicitly, so that the hearer takes it to himself and knows what is meant by it — as when someone says «How ugly is stinginess!», so [the hearer] knows that you meant to tell him: you are stingy; and as when someone said to another: «My mother was not an adulteress», insinuating that the other's mother was an adulteress. Taʿrīḍ is in any case a kind of kināya (allusion). Among its poetic examples is the saying of al-Ḥajjāj, insinuating against the governors who preceded him:
لست براعي إبل ولا غنم ... ولا بجزار على ظهر وضم
(I am no herdsman of camels or sheep, nor a butcher at the back of a chopping-block.)

farraa:1-1.t:
His words, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿ويْلٌ لِّكُلِّ هُمَزَةٍ لُّمَزَةٍ﴾.
It was revealed only concerning one man who used to يهمز and يلمز people: to backbite them and find fault with them. It is permissible in Arabic to mention something general while you intend a single one of it; you would say in ordinary speech, when a man says: I will never visit you, — you say: كل من لم يزرنى فلست بزائره (whoever does not visit me, I will not visit him), meaning it as a reply and intending him. In the reading of ʿAbd Allāh [Translator's note: Ibn Masʿūd] it is: "وَيْلٌ لِلْهُمَزَةِ اللُّمَزَةِ".

farraa:2-2.t:
His words, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿ٱلَّذِى جَمَعَ مَالاً﴾.
Al-Aʿmash and Abū Jaʿfar al-Madanī made it heavy: «جمّع»; ʿĀṣim, Nāfiʿ and al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī made it light. They all agreed on ﴿وَعَدَّدَهُ﴾ with shadda, meaning: he counted it. Al-Ḥasan read it "وعدَدَه", light; and some of them said, concerning the one who read it light: he gathered wealth and counted his number (عدده) — light — meaning his kinsfolk.

farraa:3-3.t:
His words, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿يَحْسَبُ أَنَّ مَالَهُ أَخْلَدَهُ﴾.
He means: يخلده (will make him immortal). You might say to a man: أتحسب أنّ مالك أنجاك من عذاب الله؟ ما أنجاك من عذابه إلاّ الطاعة (Do you think your wealth has saved you from Allah's punishment? Nothing has saved you from His punishment except obedience), and you mean: ما ينجيك (nothing will save you). Of the same kind is your saying of a man who commits a ruinous sin: دخل والله النار (By Allah, he has entered the Fire), and the meaning is: the Fire has become due to him.

farraa:4-4.t:
His words, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿لَيُنبَذَنَّ فِي ٱلْحُطَمَةِ﴾.
The generality read it: "لَيُنْبَذَنَّ", in the singular, and al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī alone read it [148/b] "لَيُنْبَذَانِّ فى الحطمة" (the two shall surely be flung into al-Ḥuṭama), meaning: the man and his wealth. «الحطمة» is one of the names of the Fire, like His saying: جهنم, سقر and لظى. If you dropped the alif and lām from it, since it is a proper name, it would not take tanwīn (lam yajri, i.e. it would be a diptote).

farraa:7-7.t:
His words, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿تَطَّلِعُ عَلَى ٱلأَفْئِدَةِ﴾.
He says: its pain reaches the hearts. «الاطلاع» and «البلوغ» (reaching) may have one meaning. The Arabs say: متى طلعتَ أرضنا (when did you reach our land?) and طلعتُ أرضى (I reached my land), i.e.: reached.

farraa:8-8.t:
His words, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿مُّؤْصَدَةٌ﴾.
It is the one closed over [them]; it is pronounced with hamza and without hamza.

farraa:9-9.t:
His words, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فِي عَمَدٍ مُّمَدَّدَةِ﴾.
[Abū al-ʿAbbās narrated to us; he said: Muḥammad narrated to us;] he said: al-Farrāʾ narrated to us; he said: Ismāʿīl ibn Jaʿfar al-Madanī narrated to me; he said: Our companions used to read: (فى عَمَد) with fatḥa [Translator's note: the source says «بالنصب», i.e. with fatḥa on the ʿayn and mīm], and so did al-Ḥasan. And al-Kisāʾī narrated it to me from Sulaymān ibn Arqam, from al-Ḥasan: (فى عَمَد).
[Abū al-ʿAbbās narrated to us; he said: Muḥammad narrated to us;] he said: al-Farrāʾ narrated to us; he said: Qays ibn al-Rabīʿ narrated to me from Abū Isḥāq, from ʿĀṣim ibn Ḍamra al-Salūlī, from ʿAlī, may Allah have mercy on him, that he read it: "فى عُمُد مُمَدَّدَةٍ".
[Abū al-ʿAbbās narrated to us; he said: Muḥammad narrated to us;] he said: al-Farrāʾ narrated to us; he said: Muḥammad ibn al-Faḍl narrated to me from ʿAṭāʾ, from Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd and Zayd ibn Thābit, that they both read: "فى عُمُد مُمَدَّدَة".
Al-Farrāʾ said: «العُمُد» and «العَمَد» are two plurals of «العمود» (pillar), like: الأديم, الأُدُم and الأَدَم (hide); الإهَاب, الأُهُب and الأَهَب (skin); and القضيم, القَضَم and القُضُم. And it is said: they are pillars of fire.

harrat-mujtaba:1-1.t: «ويل»: mubtadaʾ (subject); beginning with an indefinite noun is permitted because it is an imprecation (duʿāʾ); «لمزة» is a naʿt (adjective).

harrat-mujtaba:3-3.t: The clause «يحسب» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the fāʿil (agent) of «عدَّده», and the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) stands in place of the two objects of حسب.

harrat-mujtaba:4-4.t: (كلا لينبذن في الحطمة) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The clause is the answer to the oath (jawāb al-qasam), and the implied oath clause is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:5-5.t: The clause «وما أدراك» is resumptive, and the clause «ما الحطمة» is the second mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of «أدراك».

harrat-mujtaba:6-6.t: «نار»: khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e.: هي (it); the clause is resumptive; «الموقدة»: naʿt (adjective).

harrat-mujtaba:8-8.t: (إنها عليهم مؤصدة) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The preposition «عليهم» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «مؤصدة», and the clause is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:9-9.t: The preposition «في عمد» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted second khabar (predicate) of «إن».

mekki-muskil:1-1.t: His saying, Exalted is He (ويل لكل همزة): (ويل) is nominative (marfūʿ) as mubtadaʾ (subject), and that is the preferred choice. Its being accusative is permissible, as a maṣdar (verbal noun) or by way of incitement (ighrāʾ). Its explanation has already passed.

mekki-muskil:2-2.t:
His saying (الذي جمع مالا): (الذي) is in the position of the nominative on the implication of a mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. «هو الذي»; or in the position of the accusative on [the implication of] «أعني» (I mean); or in the position of the genitive (khafḍ) as a badal (substitute) for (كل).
His saying (وعدده): (عدد) is a past verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa. Al-Ḥasan read it without doubling, so it is accusative, conjoined to (مال), i.e. «وجمع عدده» (and gathered its number). It is not good for it to be, in the meaning of the doubled form, a past verb with the doubling resolved [i.e. «عَدَدَه»], because resolving the doubling in something like this is not permissible except in poetry.

mekki-muskil:3-3.t:
His saying (يحسب أن ماله أخلده): (أنّ) stands in for the two objects of (حسب).
The kasra and fatḥa of the sīn in (يحسب) are two well-known dialects. It is related that the kasra is the dialect of the Prophet ﷺ, and it is permissible in every imperfect verb from (حسب).

mekki-muskil:4-4.t: His saying (لينبذن): this verb and its like are indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa because of the nūn adjoining it, and it contains a pronoun referring to (الذي). Al-Ḥasan read «لينبذانّ» in the dual, referring it back to the wealth and its owner; and it is related from him [that he read] «لينبذُنّ» with ḍamma on the dhāl, in the plural, referring it back to the backbiter (al-humaza), the slanderer (al-lumaza) and the wealth.

mekki-muskil:5-5.t: His saying (وما أدراك ما الحطمة): its mention has already preceded.

mekki-muskil:6-6.t: His saying (نار الله): nominative (marfūʿ) on the implication of «هي»; a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate).

mekki-muskil:8-8.t: His saying (مؤصدة): whoever gave it a hamza took it from «آصدت الباب» when you have closed the door, a known dialect. Whoever did not give it a hamza made it a lightened form of the hamza; and it is possible that he took it from «أوصدت», a well-known dialect in it. It is like their saying «وكّدت» and «أكّدت», and «التأكيد» and «التوكيد», with one meaning; and likewise «أرّخت الكتاب» and «ورّخته» (I dated the letter), two dialects. His saying (بالوصيد) indicates «أوصدت» with wāw; had it been from «آصدت», it would have been «بالأصيد».

mekki-muskil:9-9.t: His saying (في عمد): whoever read it with two fatḥas made it a collective noun (ism li-l-jamʿ), because the pattern of «فعول», «فعيل» and «فعال» is to be pluralised on «فُعُل», such as «كتاب» and «كتب», «رسول» and «رسل», «رغيف» and «رغف». They also said «أديم» and «أدم», «أفيق» and «أفق»; so this is on a par with «عمود» and «عمد» with fatḥa.

muyesser-irab:1-1.t:
﴿ويل﴾: mubtadaʾ (subject).
﴿لكل﴾: the lām is a preposition, and «كل» is a noun genitive (majrūr) by the lām, the sign of its genitive being the kasra; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted khabar (predicate) of ﴿ويل﴾, and «كل» is muḍāf.
﴿همزة﴾: muḍāf ilayhi, genitive by the kasra.
﴿لمزة﴾: a naʿt (adjective) of ﴿همزة﴾, genitive by the kasra; the clause is initial (ibtidāʾiyya), with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:2-2.t:
﴿الذي﴾: a relative noun indeclinable (mabnī) on the sukūn, in the position of genitive as a badal (substitute) for ﴿كل﴾; or in the position of nominative as khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), its implied form being "he" (هو); or in the position of accusative as mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of an omitted verb, by way of censure (dhamm), i.e. "I censure the one who" (أذم الذي).
﴿جمع﴾: a past verb indeclinable on the fatḥa, and the agent is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "he" (هو); the clause ﴿جمع﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, with no grammatical position.
﴿مالا﴾: mafʿūl bihi, accusative (manṣūb) by the fatḥa.
﴿وعدده﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and «عدده» is a past verb indeclinable on the fatḥa, and the agent is latent, its implied form being "he" (هو), and the hāʾ is a pronoun indeclinable on the ḍamma in the position of accusative as mafʿūl bihi; the clause ﴿عدده﴾ is conjoined to the clause ﴿جمع﴾, with no grammatical position. The clause ﴿الذي جمع...﴾, on the implied reading ﴿هو الذي...﴾, has no grammatical position, being a resumption by way of explanation (istiʾnāf bayānī); and on the implied reading ﴿أذم الذي...﴾, it is resumptive, with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:3-3.t:
﴿يحسب﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) by the ḍamma, and the agent is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "he" (هو).
﴿أن﴾: an abrogating particle indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa, with no grammatical position.
﴿ماله﴾: the noun (ism) of «أن», accusative (manṣūb) by the fatḥa, and the hāʾ is a pronoun indeclinable on the ḍamma in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi.
﴿أخلده﴾: a past verb indeclinable on the fatḥa, and the agent is latent, its implied form being "it" (هو), and the hāʾ is a pronoun indeclinable on the ḍamma in the position of accusative as mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause ﴿أخلده﴾ is in the position of nominative as the khabar (predicate) of «أن»; the clause ﴿أن ماله أخلده﴾ stands in place of the two objects of «يحسب»; and the clause ﴿يحسب...﴾ is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the agent of «جمع» or from the agent of «عدده», i.e. "reckoning that the wealth will make him immortal" (حاسبًا أن المال سيخلده); or it is a resumption by way of explanation (istiʾnāf bayānī), with no grammatical position, as if it were asked: "What is the matter with him that he gathers wealth and is preoccupied with it?" (ما باله يجمع المال ويهتم به؟)

muyesser-irab:4-4.t:
﴿كلا﴾: a particle of deterrence and rebuke.
﴿لينبذن﴾: the lām is the answer of an omitted oath, and «ينبذن» is an imperfect verb in the passive (lit. "whose agent is not named"), indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa because it is joined to the heavy nūn of emphasis, and the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "he" (هو); the clause has no grammatical position, because it is the answer of the oath.
﴿في الحطمة﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿لينبذن﴾; the oath clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:5-5.t:
﴿وما﴾: the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya), and «ما» is an interrogative noun indeclinable (mabnī) on the sukūn, in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject).
﴿أدراك﴾: a past verb indeclinable on the fatḥa implied (muqaddar) on the alif, and the agent is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "it" (هو), referring back to «ما»; the kāf is the pronoun of the addressee, indeclinable on the fatḥa, in the position of accusative as first mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause ﴿أدراك﴾ is in the position of nominative as the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ ﴿ما﴾.
﴿ما﴾: an interrogative noun indeclinable on the sukūn, in the position of nominative as mubtadaʾ.
﴿الحطمة﴾: khabar of the mubtadaʾ, nominative (marfūʿ) by the ḍamma; the nominal clause ﴿ما الحطمة﴾ is in the position of accusative, standing in place of the second and third objects of ﴿أدراك﴾, and the clause ﴿وما أدراك ...﴾ is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from His saying ﴿الحطمة﴾ in the previous ayah, the link (rābiṭ) being the repetition of the word «الحطمة».

muyesser-irab:6-6.t:
﴿نار﴾: khabar (predicate), nominative (marfūʿ) by the ḍamma, of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), its implied form being "it" (هي), i.e. "it is the fire of Allah" (هي نار الله); the nominal clause is a resumption by way of explanation (istiʾnāf bayānī), so it has no grammatical position. Or: ﴿نار﴾ is a badal (substitute) for «الحطمة», nominative by the ḍamma. «نار» is muḍāf.
﴿الله﴾: the Name of Majesty, muḍāf ilayhi, genitive (majrūr), the sign of its genitive being the kasra.
﴿الموقدة﴾: a naʿt (adjective) of «النار», nominative by the ḍamma.

muyesser-irab:7-7.t:
﴿التي﴾: a relative noun indeclinable (mabnī) on the sukūn, in the position of nominative as a second naʿt (adjective) of ﴿نار﴾. Or: in the position of nominative as khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. "it is the one which" (هي التي).
﴿تطلع﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) by the ḍamma, and the agent is latent (mustatir), its implied form being "it" (هي), referring back to the fire; the clause ﴿تطلع﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, with no grammatical position.
﴿على الأفئدة﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿تطلع﴾; the clause ﴿التي تطلع...﴾, on the implied reading ﴿هي التي تطلع...﴾, is resumptive, with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:8-8.t:
﴿إنها﴾: «إن» is an abrogating particle indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa, with no grammatical position, and ﴿ها﴾ is a pronoun indeclinable on the sukūn in the position of accusative as the noun (ism) of «إن».
﴿عليهم﴾: «على» is a preposition, the hāʾ is a pronoun indeclinable on the kasra in the position of genitive, and the mīm is the sign of the plural; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿مؤصدة﴾.
﴿مؤصدة﴾: the khabar (predicate) of «إن», nominative (marfūʿ) by the ḍamma; the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position.

muyesser-irab:9-9.t:
﴿في عمد﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial), either from the pronoun in ﴿عليهم﴾, i.e. "bound in columns of iron, shackled with them", or from the pronoun in ﴿إنها﴾, i.e. "the kindled fire is in columns". Or they are attached to a second khabar (predicate) of «إن», or to the khabar of a concealed mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. "it is in columns" (هي في عمد), or "they are in columns" (هم في عمد).
﴿ممددة﴾: a naʿt (adjective) of ﴿عمد﴾, genitive (majrūr) by the kasra; the clause, on the implied reading "it is in columns" (هي في عمد) or "they are in columns" (هم في عمد), is resumptive, with no grammatical position.

nahhas-irab:1-1.t:
وَيْلٌ is nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject). Its accusative is permissible, because it is in the sense of a maṣdar (verbal noun), just as قبوحا له ("ugliness to him!") is permissible in the accusative; except that the nominative in «ويل» is better, because it is not derived from a verb, and the accusative in قبوح is better, because it is derived from a verb. There is another view on the accusative of «ويل»: the implied form is "say: may Allah attach woe (wayl) to every slanderer", and this is the position of Sībawayh.
Mujāhid said: This is not specific to anyone. Abū Jaʿfar said: This is a correct view in Arabic, because the way of كلّ is to be non-specific. Abū al-ʿĀliya said: «al-humaza» is the one who finds fault with people to their faces, and al-lumaza is the one who finds fault with them behind their backs.
I heard ʿAlī ibn Sulaymān approve of this view. Ibn Zayd said: al-humaza is the one who jabs (yahmizu) people and strikes them with his hand, and al-lumaz is the one who taunts them and finds fault with them with his tongue.

nahhas-irab:2-2.t:
الَّذِي is in the position of the nominative in the sense of "he is the one who"; the accusative is permissible in the sense of "I mean the one who", and the genitive is permissible as a badal (substitute) for كلّ. Abū Jaʿfar, Yaḥyā ibn Waththāb, al-Aʿmash, Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī read «جمّع» with doubling, and al-Ḥasan, Ibn Kathīr, ʿĀṣim, Abū ʿAmr, Shayba and Nāfiʿ read جَمَعَ. Abū Jaʿfar said: «جمع» without doubling is for little and much, and جمّع is only for much.
It is narrated from al-Ḥasan: وَعَدَدَهُ without doubling [Translator's note: the printed text has the standard وَعَدَّدَهُ], and it is an anomalous (shādhdh) reading if he means عدّه with the doubling then made overt (iẓhār al-taḍʿīf), as the poet said: [al-Basīṭ] 585- إنّي أجود لأقوام وإن ضننوا ("I am generous to people, even if they are stingy") — and this is far-fetched, permissible only in poetry. But if he means "he gathered wealth and gathered its number (ʿadadahu)", as an object, i.e., counted its number, then it is permissible.

nahhas-irab:3-4.t: يَحْسَبُ أَنَّ مالَهُ أَخْلَدَهُ (3): it is said: it is the dialect of the Prophet ﷺ, with kasra on the sīn (يحسِب), coming on the pattern faʿila yafʿilu; it has a few parallels which we have mentioned. «أنّ» and what it governs are in the position of the two objects. What is known of the reading of al-Ḥasan is «لينبذانّ في الحطمة», he and his wealth; and (لينبذُنّ) with ḍamma on the dhāl has also been narrated from him. It was said: this is not permissible, because only two have been mentioned before; and it was said: it is for the humaza, the lumaza, and the one who gathered wealth.

nahhas-irab:5-5.t:
Al-Farrāʾ said: (al-Ḥuṭama is) a name of the Fire, and if it were without alif-lām it would be a diptote. Abū Jaʿfar said:
One says ḥaṭamahu when he breaks it, as the poet said: [al-Rajaz] 586- قد لفّها اللّيل بسوّاق حطم ("the night has wrapped them in a fierce (ḥuṭam) driver"); and a ḥuṭam man, i.e., a voracious eater.

nahhas-irab:6-7.t: نارُ اللَّهِ, i.e., it is the fire of Allah. «الموقدة» is a naʿt (adjective) of the fire, and likewise الَّتِي تَطَّلِعُ عَلَى الْأَفْئِدَةِ (7). Iṭṭalaʿtu ʿalā fulān and ṭalaʿtu, i.e., I reached. The singular of الأفئدة is fuʾād.

nahhas-irab:8-8.t: (مؤصدة is) the khabar (predicate) of «إن». One says āṣadtu and awṣadtu: whoever says awṣadtu says mūṣada, without hamza, and whoever says āṣadtu says muʾṣada; and it is permissible to lighten the hamza and say mūṣada. Both dialects are good and widespread. Likewise akkadtu and wakkadtu, i.e., al-taʾkīd and al-tawkīd; likewise arrakhtu and warrakhtu, i.e., al-taʾrīkh and al-tawrīkh; and ākaftu and awkaftu, i.e., al-ikāf and al-wikāf (pack-saddle).

nahhas-irab:9-9.t:
فِي عَمَدٍ: thus (فِي عُمُدٍ) it is narrated from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, may Allah be pleased with him, Ibn Masʿūd and Zayd ibn Thābit, and it is the reading of ʿĀṣim [Translator's note: so in the text; ʿĀṣim in the transmission of Ḥafṣ reads عَمَدٍ], Yaḥyā ibn Waththāb, al-Aʿmash, Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī; and the Medinans and Abū ʿAmr read فِي عَمَدٍ [Translator's note: the printed vowelling is the same in both places; the first reading is عُمُد, with ḍamma, the second عَمَد, with fatḥa]. When something comes with such agreement (of transmitters), religion forbids saying:
one of the two is better than the other. The best that has been said is: thus it was revealed, as the Prophet ﷺ said: «The Qur'an was revealed in seven aḥruf, all of them healing and sufficient». But the readings are analysed from (the standpoint of) Arabic: one says ʿamūd and ʿumud; thus faʿūl, faʿīl and fiʿāl form their plural on fuʿul, as in kitāb and kutub, raghīf and rughuf. And they said adīm and adam, and this, like ʿamūd and ʿamad, is a collective noun, not a true plural; likewise afīq and afaq, ihāb and ahab, naʿīm and naʿam; and they said khādim and khadam.
As for the meaning of «في عمد», the exegetes and the scholars of Arabic have discussed it. ʿAṭāʾ al-Khurāsānī said: it means pillars of fire extended over them. Ibn Zayd said: فِي عَمَدٍ مُمَدَّدَةٍ, i.e., they are shackled with pillars of iron which have burned and become fire. It has been said: the doors are closed upon them, i.e., shut tight, and pillars of iron are set up on them, so that this may be more severe for their despair of getting out. It has been said: «في عمد» means among pillars, as you say "so-and-so is in (fī) the people", i.e., among them. And it has been said: (it means) with pillars, as the poet said: [al-Ṭawīl] 587-
وهل ينعمن من كان آخر عهده ... ثلاثين شهرا في ثلاثة أحوال
(Can one live in comfort whose last acquaintance [with the place] was thirty months in three years?)
i.e., with (maʿa). I heard ʿAlī ibn Sulaymān say: «في» is in its proper meaning, i.e., thirty months contained within three years.
Abū Jaʿfar said: Among the most important things narrated on the verse is what is narrated from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, may Allah be pleased with him; he said: "Do you know what the gates of the Fire are like?" We said: "Like these doors of ours." He said: "No; they are one above another." «ممدّدة» in the genitive is a naʿt (adjective) of عمد, and in the nominative a naʿt of موصدة, or a khabar after a khabar.

semin-durr:1-1.t:
His saying: {هُمَزَةٍ}: that is, one who does much hamz (backbiting by gesture or word); likewise «اللُّمَزَة» is one who does much lamz (slander). The meaning of hamz was treated in [Sūrat] Nūn, and lamz in [Sūrat] Barāʾa. The majority read the mīm with fatḥa, on the footing that what is meant is the person from whom that act is frequent. Ziyād al-Aʿjam said:
4640 - تُدْلِي بِوْدِّيْ إذا لا قَيْتَني كَذِباً ... وإنْ أُغَيَّبْ فأنتَ الهامِزُ اللُّمَزَةْ
(You offer me your friendship, falsely, when you meet me; and if I am absent, you are the backbiter, the slanderer.)
Al-Bāqir read with sukūn, meaning one at whom hamz and lamz are directed, that is, one who brings about what causes people to backbite and slander him, like «ḍuḥaka» for one who laughs much, and «ḍuḥka» for one at whom people laugh because of what he does. This is regular; I mean that the form fuʿala with fatḥa on the ʿayn is for one from whom the act is frequent, and with sukūn for one on account of whom the act occurs.

semin-durr:2-2.t:
His saying: {الذى جَمَعَ}: it may be put in the genitive as a badal (substitute), and in the accusative or the nominative by disjunction (qaṭʿ). It may not be put in the genitive as an adjective (naʿt) or an explicative apposition (bayān), because the two differ in definiteness and indefiniteness. As for His saying «جَمَعَ»: the two brothers (Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī) and Ibn ʿĀmir read it with shadda on the mīm, for intensity and multiplication, and because it agrees with «عَدَّدَه»; the others read «جمَعَ» without shadda, which admits both multiplication and its absence.
His saying «وعَدَّدَه»: the majority read it with the first dāl doubled, which is also for intensity. Al-Ḥasan and al-Kalbī read it without doubling. There are several views on it. The first: the meaning is "he gathered wealth and counted that wealth", that is, "and he gathered its number", that is, he reckoned it. The second: the meaning is "and he gathered the number of his own people from his clan and relatives". On these two interpretations «عَدَدَه» is a noun conjoined to «مالاً», that is, "and he gathered the number of the wealth" or "the number of his own people". The third: that «عَدَدَه» is a past verb meaning "he counted it" (ʿaddahu), except that it is irregular in being left unassimilated, as it is irregular in the saying:
4641 -. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ...
إني أَجُوْدُ لأَِقْوامٍ وإنْ ضَنِنُوا
(. . . I am generous to people, even if they are stingy.)

semin-durr:3-3.t: His saying: {يَحْسَبُ}: it may be resumptive (mustaʾnafa), and it may be a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the agent of «جَمَعَ». As for «أَخْلَدَه», it means «يُخْلِدُه» ("will make him immortal"), the past having been put in the place of the imperfect. It was also said that it is in its original sense, that is: "it prolonged his life".

semin-durr:4-4.t:
His saying: {لَيُنبَذَنَّ}: the answer to an implied oath. ʿAlī, may Allah be pleased with him, al-Ḥasan (with a disagreement reported from him), Ibn Muḥayṣin and Abū ʿAmr in one report read «ليُنْبَذانِّ» with the alif of the dual, that is, "he and his wealth will both be cast". From al-Ḥasan also: «لَيُنْبَذُنَّ» with ḍamma on the dhāl, attributed to a plural pronoun, that is: "we shall surely cast the backbiter and his supporters".
Al-ḥuṭama is one who does much shattering (al-ḥaṭm). One says "a ḥuṭama man", that is, a glutton; and "ḥaṭamtuhu" means "I broke it"; and al-ḥuṭām (broken pieces) is from it. He said:
4642 - قد لَفَّها الليلُ بسَوَّاقٍ حُطَمْ
(Night has wrapped it up with a harsh, crushing driver.)
And another said:
4643 - إنَّا حَطَمْنا بالقضيبِ مُصْعَباً ... يومَ كسَرْنا أَنْفَه لِيَغْضَبا
(We smashed Muṣʿab with the rod, the day we broke his nose that he might be angered.)
His saying «نارُ الله»: that is, "it is the fire of Allah".

semin-durr:7-7.t:
His saying: {التي تَطَّلِعُ}: it may be a follower (tābiʿa) of «نارُ الله», and it may be disjoined (maqṭūʿa). . .

[Translator's note: the source entry breaks off here with an ellipsis; it is translated as it stands.]

semin-durr:9-9.t: His saying: {فِي عَمَدٍ}: the two brothers and Abū Bakr read it with two ḍammas, as the plural of «عَمُود» (column), like «rasūl» and «rusul». It was also said to be the plural of «ʿimād», like «kitāb» and «kutub». From Abū ʿAmr it is reported with ḍamma and sukūn, a lightening of this reading. The others read «عَمَد» with two fatḥas. It was said to be a collective noun (ism jamʿ) for «ʿamūd». It was also said that it is rather a plural of it; al-Farrāʾ said: like «adīm» and «adam». Abū ʿUbayda said: "It is the plural of «ʿimād»." «في عَمَدٍ» may be a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in «عليهم», that is, "bound fast"; or the khabar of an implied mubtadaʾ, that is, "they are in columns"; or an attribute of «مُؤْصَدَة». Abū l-Baqāʾ said: "that is, the fire would then be inside the columns."

ukberi-tibyan:1-3.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَيْلٌ لِكُلِّ هُمَزَةٍ لُمَزَةٍ (١) الَّذِي جَمَعَ مَالًا وَعَدَّدَهُ (٢) يَحْسَبُ أَنَّ مَالَهُ أَخْلَدَهُ (٣)).
The «hāʾ» [i.e. the tāʾ marbūṭa] in «الْهُمَزَة» and «اللُّمَزَة» is for intensification (mubālagha).
(الَّذِي) may be genitive as a badal (substitute), accusative by an implied «أَعْنِي» (I mean), or nominative on [the implied] «هُوَ» (he is).
(عَدَّدَهُ) is with a doubled consonant, as a verb, either from «الْعَدَد» (counting) or from «الْإِعْدَاد» (preparing).
(يَحْسَبُ) is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in «جَمَعَ». (أَخْلَدَهُ) is in the sense of «يُخَلِّدُهُ» (will make him immortal). It is also said that it is in its proper sense, i.e. it lengthened his life.

ukberi-tibyan:4-4.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (كَلَّا لَيُنْبَذَنَّ فِي الْحُطَمَةِ (٤)).
The words of the Exalted (لَيُنْبَذَنَّ): i.e. the one who amasses. [It is also read] «لَيُنْبَذَانِّ», i.e. he and his wealth; and «لَيُنْبَذُنَّ» with a ḍamma on the dhāl, i.e. he, his wealth and his counting [of it] as well; and it may be that the meaning is he and his various kinds of wealth, because they are diverse.

ukberi-tibyan:6-9.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (نَارُ اللَّهِ الْمُوقَدَةُ (٦) الَّتِي تَطَّلِعُ عَلَى الْأَفْئِدَةِ (٧) إِنَّهَا عَلَيْهِمْ مُؤْصَدَةٌ (٨) فِي عَمَدٍ مُمَدَّدَةٍ (٩)).
The words of the Exalted (نَارُ اللَّهِ): i.e. «هِيَ نَارُ اللَّهِ» (it is the fire of Allah). (الَّتِي) is nominative as a naʿt (adjective), or the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), or in the position of the accusative by «أَعْنِي» (I mean).
(الْأَفْئِدَةِ) is a plural of paucity (jamʿ qilla) used in place of [a plural of] multitude. «الْعَمَد» with a fatḥa is the plural of «عَمُود» or «عِمَاد» (pillar), and it is a rare plural.
It is said that it is also read with two ḍammas, like «كِتَاب» and «كُتُب», «رَسُول» and «رُسُل». The implied form is: «هُمْ فِي عَمَدٍ» (they are in pillars). It may also be a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the genitive pronoun, i.e. bound fast; and it may be a ṣifa (adjective) of «مُؤْصَدَة». And Allah knows best.

zajjaj:1-1.t:
Sūrat al-Humaza
Meccan
﷽
His saying: ﴿وَيْلٌ لِكُلِّ هُمَزَةٍ لُمَزَةٍ﴾ ("woe to every slanderer, backbiter"): ”وَيْلٌ“ is nominative (marfūʿ) as mubtadaʾ (subject), and the khabar (predicate) is ﴿لِكُلِّ هُمَزَةٍ﴾. If it were outside the Qur'an the accusative would be permissible, but it is not permissible in the Qur'an because it would contradict the Muṣḥaf. Whoever says ”وَيْلًا لِلْكافِرِينَ“ ("woe to the unbelievers", accusative), the meaning is: "Allah has assigned him woe"; and whoever says ”وَيْلٌ“, that is better in Arabic, because woe has been established for him. ”اَلْوَيْلُ“ is a word said to everyone who has fallen into ruin. ”اَلْهُمَزَةُ اللُّمَزَةُ“ is the one who backbites people and disparages them. The poet said:
إذا لَقِيتُكَ عَنْ كُرْهٍ تُكاشِرُنِي ∗∗∗ وإنْ تَغَيَّبْتُ كُنْتَ الهامِزَ اللُّمَزَةْ
(When I meet you, you grin at me grudgingly; and if I am absent, you are the slanderer, the backbiter.)
It was read: ”اَلَّذِي جَمَّعَ مالًا“ ("who amassed wealth", with doubling), and it was read: ﴿جَمَعَ مالا﴾ [al-Humaza: 2] with the light [mīm]. And it was read: ﴿وَعَدَّدَهُ﴾ [al-Humaza: 2] with the doubled [dāl], and it was read: ”وَعَدَدَهُ“ with the light [dāl]. Whoever reads ﴿وَعَدَّدَهُ﴾ [al-Humaza: 2], its meaning is: and counted it [as provision] for the ages; and whoever reads ﴿وَعَدَّدَهُ﴾ [al-Humaza: 2], its meaning is: he gathered wealth and numbers (ʿadad), that is, and people whom he prepared as helpers. [Translator's note: the second ﴿وَعَدَّدَهُ﴾ is evidently meant to be the light reading «وَعَدَدَهُ», as the explanation "wealth and numbers" shows.]

zajjaj:3-3.t: And His saying: ﴿يَحْسَبُ أنَّ مالَهُ أخْلَدَهُ﴾ ("he thinks that his wealth has made him immortal"): that is, he acts as one acts who, with his affluence, does not think that he will die.

zajjaj:4-4.t: And His saying: ﴿لَيُنْبَذَنَّ في الحُطَمَةِ﴾ ("he will surely be flung into the Crusher"): that is, he will be thrown into the Fire. ”اَلْحُطَمَةُ“ is one of the names of the Fire. It was also read: ”لَيُنْبَذانِّ في الحُطَمَةِ“ (dual), and it is related from al-Ḥasan, on the meaning: "he and his wealth will surely be flung into the Crusher". And it was read: ”لَتُنْبَذُنَّ في الحُطَمَةِ“, whose meaning is that he will be flung, he and what he gathered, into the Crusher. [Translator's note: so in the source; the vowelling of «لَتُنْبَذُنَّ» as printed (second person) does not match the explanation given, and may be corrupt.] The well-known reading is ﴿لَيُنْبَذَنَّ﴾.

zajjaj:6-7.t: His saying: ﴿نارُ اللَّهِ المُوقَدَةُ﴾ ﴿الَّتِي تَطَّلِعُ عَلى الأفْئِدَةِ﴾ ("the kindled Fire of Allah, which rises over the hearts"): this is a Fire prepared for these unbelievers and those like them. And the meaning of ﴿تَطَّلِعُ عَلى الأفْئِدَةِ﴾ is: its pain and its burning reach the hearts.

zajjaj:8-8.t: And His saying: ﴿إنَّها عَلَيْهِمْ مُؤْصَدَةٌ﴾ ("it will be closed down upon them"): it was read with hamza and without hamza; it was read ”مُوصَدَةٌ“. The Arabs say ”أوْصَدْتُهُ“, and according to this it is ”مُوصَدَةٌ“; and they say ”آصَدْتُهُ“, and according to this it is ”مُؤْصَدَةٌ“ with hamza. The meaning of ”مُوصَدَةٌ“ is "closed over", that is, the punishment is closed over them.

zajjaj:9-9.t: And His saying: ﴿فِي عَمَدٍ مُمَدَّدَةٍ﴾ ("in extended columns"): it was also read ”فِي عُمُدٍ“. It is the plural of ”عِمادٌ“: ”عُمَدٌ“ and ”عُمُدٌ“, as they said ”إهابٌ“ ("hide"), ”أُهَبٌ“ and ”أُهُبٌ“. Its meaning is that it is in columns of fire. [Translator's note: the source vowels the first plural «عُمَدٌ»; the Qur'anic reading discussed is «عَمَدٍ».]
